assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology and GLP-1 biology led to a new drug class that has transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity treatment and is showing benefit in cardiovascular, renal and other outcomes. The discovery chain (proglucagon processing, GLP-1 as insulinotropic and satiety signal, stabilised analogues) is clear, original and of very large clinical and physiological impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 and incretin effect), Drucker (GLP-1 receptor biology, GLP-2 and translational work) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 peptide form) form a plausible trio. Knudsen's role is largely drug development and could be seen as industrial rather than discovery credit; other early contributors outside the list (as I recall, Habener) may complicate allocation. Mojsov's credit is debated in the literature.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved agents and large outcome trials; recognition is timely and arguably overdue given the scale of benefit.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among early peptide-identification contributors is contested and I have not verified details.
Whether the committee prefers to recognise physiology/discovery rather than drug development.
Long-term safety and durability of obesity treatment still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed against tumour antigens created a new modality of cancer therapy, with durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemias and lymphomas and now myeloma. Strong conceptual originality, immunological relevance and clear clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CAR design with co-stimulation and preclinical proof), June (clinical translation and 4-1BB CARs in CLL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T cells) are decisive; Eshhar and others outside the list may be viewed as precursors, so the trio is defensible but not unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products, years of follow-up and independent confirmation; limitations in solid tumours and toxicity are known but do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Priority among early CAR concepts (including contributors not on the list) is unresolved.
Efficacy in solid tumours remains limited.
Secondary malignancy and toxicity signals still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstration that TNF is a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis and that its blockade produces clinical benefit changed the course of rheumatology and extended to IBD, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis. A textbook example of bench-to-bedside discovery with lasting impact, and the concept of cytokine-targeted therapy that followed.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly drove the mechanistic rationale and the first clinical trials, which makes a clean two-person configuration. Other contributors to TNF biology and antibody engineering exist but the therapeutic proof of concept is clearly theirs.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty-five years of clinical use, many biosimilars, wide independent confirmation; recognition is mature and possibly late.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as clinical development rather than a fundamental discovery.
Contribution of TNF discovery itself (Cerami, Old, Beutler) is separate and not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational targeting of BCR-ABL turned chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a chronic manageable one and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. Originality and impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical leadership and trials), Lydon (compound development and kinase inhibitor concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are all decisive; Rowley, Nowell, Witte and others laid the oncogene groundwork, which complicates the credit story.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of outcome data, resistance mechanisms understood, independent replication; fully mature.
uncertainties: Competing credit for the underlying oncogene discovery and kinase biology.
Whether translational/industrial roles are appropriate for a Nobel configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, which has dramatically changed outcomes in a lethal childhood disease. It is a clear example of an RNA-mechanism-based therapeutic and a proof of principle for antisense drugs.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO design for SMN2 exon 7) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) form a natural pair. Other groups, including Hua and Singh in Krainer's lab and earlier splicing-modulation work, may deserve acknowledgement.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term follow-up and independent trial confirmation; recognition is reasonably timely, though competing modalities (gene therapy, risdiplam) are evolving.
uncertainties: Relative weight of the splicing-mechanism discovery versus the drug-development contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defined how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immune and interferon responses, with relevance to viral infection, autoimmunity (including interferonopathies and lupus), cancer immunity and ageing. This is a fundamental discovery with wide conceptual reach, of direct relevance to autoimmune disease mechanisms.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and cGAMP as second messenger) and Barber (STING) are the most clearly decisive; Ishikawa, Wu and Sun were key co-discoverers but a smaller configuration is more consistent with Nobel limits. Other contributors (Vance, Patel, Hornung) are outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed mechanistically; therapeutic translation (STING agonists and antagonists) is still immature, so clinical impact is more prospective.
uncertainties: Clinical translation has not yet delivered approved therapies.
Attribution between cGAS and STING discovery arms and among additional contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like-particle HPV vaccines prevent infection and cervical and other HPV-related cancers, with population-level evidence of reduced disease. It is a landmark in cancer prevention with strong global health relevance.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (L1/L2 expression and vaccine development) are plausible; Jian Zhou, who contributed to early VLP work and died in 1999, and other groups complicate allocation, and zur Hausen has already been recognised for HPV and cervical cancer.
assessment.maturity: Population effectiveness data now strong, including cancer incidence declines in vaccinated cohorts; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Competing priority claims on VLP technology.
Overlap with prior HPV recognition may reduce novelty in the committee's view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of IL-6 as a central B-cell differentiation and inflammatory cytokine, followed by tocilizumab, opened effective treatment for rheumatoid arthritis, giant-cell arteritis, cytokine release syndrome and other conditions. Clear discovery-to-therapy continuum in immune-mediated disease.
assessment.attribution: Kishimoto and Hirano cloned and characterised IL-6 and its receptor and led the therapeutic concept; the pair is clean. Others (Poupart, Content, Van Snick on parallel IL-6 forms) could be debated but are not listed.
assessment.maturity: Approved for over a decade with broad independent confirmation and COVID-19 and CAR-T toxicity uses; recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Competing parallel discovery claims for IL-6 under different names.
Possible overlap with the TNF candidate in rheumatology could limit joint recognition.
